Q1_writer_side_diagnosis.question: Did the gap-producing commits advance next_id?
Q1_writer_side_diagnosis.answer: NO. The writer wrote new items[] entries (EXP-629, EXP-630) and never bumped next_id. The bug is in the claim/write code path missing the atomic next_id++, NOT a claim-advances-then-write-overwrites-with-stale-snapshot pattern.
evidence_via_github_contents_api: 260fafd (analyst-baby EXP-629 write, 2026-06-15T03:41Z): expansion-tracker.json had next_id=627, live_max=629 — EXP-629 present in items[] but next_id NOT advanced (still 627).
ca0fd35 (analyst-baby EXP-630 write, 2026-06-15T15:37Z): next_id=627, live_max=630 — still stale.

1813a46 (analyst-baby claim EXP-631..637, 2026-06-16T03:37Z): next_id=638, live_max=637 — SELF-HEALED. The allocator took safeNext=max(declared=627, liveMax+1=631)=631, allocated 7 ids, advanced next_id to 638. PROP-100 clamp working as designed on the READ side.
Q1_writer_side_diagnosis.diagnosis: PROP-100's clamp is a READ-side self-heal: it repairs a stale next_id at the moment of the NEXT allocation. It does NOT guarantee that a writer advances next_id in lockstep with its OWN write. analyst-baby's prompt (analyst-baby.md Mode 1 BAU drain, steps 3/5/6) describes writing the consolidated tracker entry and marking originals consolidated, but contains NO shared allocation code block and NO explicit `t.next_id++` — the Sonnet model improvises the allocation each run. Sometimes it bumps next_id (1813a46), sometimes it does not (260fafd). This is the exact PROP-089 defect class: prompt-level allocation logic gets improvised/skipped under load. The fix is identical: extract a single allocator script that reserves-and-bumps atomically and a push-time lint that refuses to land a stale write.

findings.why_integrity_only_sees_a_few: Integrity runs daily (one sample/day). The median episode self-heals within hours (defensive allocator on the next write). So integrity samples ~1-2 of the 44 episodes; the other ~42 opened and self-healed inside a 24h window and were invisible to the daily check.

Q3_recurrence_rate.verdict: The directive's floor estimate ('at least 2 recurrences in 60 days') is a ~22x undercount. This is FREQUENT-SILENT, not RARE-BUT-RECURRING. That materially changes the cost-benefit: the integrity 'major' finding is not a once-a-month event, and the staleness window is open ~21% of the time. BUT — see Q7 — the same data shows the self-heal has a 100% catch rate over 60 days (zero actual collisions corrupted state), so 'frequent' does not mean 'damaging yet'.

proposal.design_principle: Same trade as PROP-089/PROP-066: move the allocation logic the Sonnet writers keep improvising out of prose and into a script invocation that is structurally hard to skip, then back it with a strict push-time invariant gate so a stale write cannot land on origin/main. Phase 1 does NOT make concurrent-run collisions mathematically impossible (two clones from the same base can still reserve the same ids locally); it makes every stale write (a) impossible to push unnoticed and (b) mechanically recoverable. Given the observed rate (~5 episodes/week, all self-healed so far) and the keep-it-simple constraint, strict-detect-at-the-git-boundary is the right cost point.

changes.what: Extract shared monitor/scripts/allocate-ids-lib.js used by BOTH allocate-iss-ids.js and the new allocate-exp-ids.js
changes.detail: Per directive constraint ('Don't duplicate'). The two allocators are structurally identical: read file, compute archive-aware max, take safeNext = max(declaredNext, liveMax+1, archMax+1) floor, reserve N contiguous ids, write next_id := safeNext+N back atomically (tmp-file + rename). The lib exports `allocate({openPathOrTrackerPath, idField, idPrefix, padWidth, archivePath, count, dryRun})`. allocate-iss-ids.js becomes a thin wrapper binding (open-issues.json, 'next_iss_id', 'ISS-', no-pad, closure-ledger+closed-issues). allocate-exp-ids.js binds (expansion-tracker.json, 'next_id', 'EXP-', pad-3, expansion-tracker-archive.jsonl). NOTE: refactoring allocate-iss-ids.js to use the shared lib is OPTIONAL for Phase 1 (it already works); if the operator prefers minimal blast radius, ship allocate-exp-ids.js standalone first and fold both into the lib in a follow-up. Recommend the shared lib only if it lands in the SAME apply session (atomic), else standalone first.
changes.classification: git-owned source code: add to build.js OWNERSHIP, workspace-sync.md NEVER_PUSH, CLAUDE.md File Ownership list — same as allocate-iss-ids.js.

changes.what: New script monitor/scripts/allocate-exp-ids.js — the ONLY supported way to mint EXP ids
changes.detail: Usage: node monitor/scripts/allocate-exp-ids.js [--count N] [--dry-run] [--verify]. Behavior mirrors allocate-iss-ids.js exactly: (1) read expansion-tracker.json; (2) archive-aware max-walk across items[] AND expansion-tracker-archive.jsonl (the PROP-100 / PROP-053-rev2 archive-aware semantics); (3) safeNext = max(next_id, liveMax+1, archMax+1) — warn on clamp; (4) reserve N contiguous ids [safeNext, safeNext+N) formatted EXP-NNN (zero-padded to 3); (5) write next_id := safeNext+N back atomically; (6) print reserved ids one per line. A crash between reserve and item-write leaves an id GAP, which is harmless (gaps are already the no_trace norm per expansion-tracker-gap-semantics.md); reuse is the only disease. --verify mode runs the invariant check only (next_id > max(all EXP ids in live ∪ archive); no duplicate EXP ids within items[]) and exits 1 with detail — shared by C3 and usable ad hoc.
changes.rationale: Q1 proved analyst-baby improvises and sometimes omits next_id++. A script call (IDS=$(node monitor/scripts/allocate-exp-ids.js --count N)) is structurally hard to skip; four prior PROPs prove the extraction pattern sticks where prose does not.

changes.what: Push-time enforcement: STRICT next_id-invariant lint, chained into ALL THREE writers' pre-push hooks
changes.detail: Q5 DECISION: a PEER script monitor/scripts/lint-exp-allocations.js, NOT an extension of lint-decider-surfaces.js. Reason: lint-decider-surfaces.js is chained ONLY into the decider's pre-push hook (PROP-083 chain), but the EXP surface is written by analyst + analyst-baby + decider — the primary gap-openers (analyst-baby) never run the decider hook. Extending lint-decider-surfaces.js would guard only decider pushes and miss the dominant writer. The peer script `node monitor/scripts/lint-exp-allocations.js` asserts the STRICT invariant: next_id > max(all EXP ids across items[] ∪ archive). It is chained into the pre-push hooks of analyst, analyst-baby, AND decider clones (the same install pattern as PROP-081's required-artifacts hook / PROP-083's lint chain). Exit 1 = block push, print the violating ids + the C4 recovery procedure. Diff-aware scoping is NOT needed for the strict invariant (the invariant is a whole-file property, and legacy gaps are no_trace not inversions, so the strict check never fires on benign reservation drift — only on the actual write-without-bump bug).
changes.rationale: This is the layer that makes a future improvised stale write non-landable. Q6 STRICT choice: parity with PROP-089's ISS next_iss_id invariant; strict (next_id > live_max) is easier to assert than per-id collision detection and catches near-misses + cross-run drift, not just active races. Other-side on strict (Q6): a writer with a summary-only / no-new-EXP commit could be blocked if the tracker is ALREADY stale from someone else's prior bad write — but that is CORRECT behavior, it forces the self-heal commit to fix the invariant before piling new commits on top. The defensive self-heal (PROP-100) stays in place as the repair mechanism that makes passing the gate a one-liner.

changes.what: Canonical concurrent-collision recovery procedure for EXP (written, mechanical)
changes.detail: Mirror PROP-089 C4. Add to analyst.md / analyst-baby.md / decider integration reference: when a push is rejected non-FF OR lint-exp-allocations.js exits 1, after `git pull --rebase`, re-run `node monitor/scripts/allocate-exp-ids.js --verify`. If it reports the invariant violated by ids YOUR run minted: (1) run allocate-exp-ids.js --count k to mint k fresh ids from the rebased state; (2) rename your k colliding new EXP records (file + items[] entry + every reference in files touched by this same commit: issue-proposals, attention-inbox, review refs); (3) re-run --verify (must pass); (4) re-push. Never renumber the OTHER writer's entries (they won the race by landing first); never decrement next_id; never delete the gap ids (they are harmless no_trace).
changes.rationale: Unwritten LLM-executed recovery is a variance generator. Canonicalize it so the next race resolves identically regardless of which of the three writers / which model hits it.

Q7_other_side_explicit.argue_against_doing_anything: The defensive allocator (PROP-100) IS the fix. Q3 shows 44 staleness episodes in 60 days yet ZERO actual collisions corrupted state — the self-heal has a 100% catch rate. The writers run on hourly+ cadences with PEAK-SHIFT non-concurrent scheduling (analyst UTC 00/04/08, analyst-baby 04:20/16:20, decider 02/06/10), so the genuine concurrent-write window inside a staleness gap is small. Strict lint adds a fail-closed gate that fires on every staleness even when no race is happening — that is the integrity 'major' finding's cost moved earlier in the pipeline, ~5x/week. One could argue the cheaper move is to DOWNGRADE the integrity check (treat next_id<=live_max as INFO not MAJOR, since the self-heal always catches it) rather than ship script+lint+hook-on-3-agents.
Q7_other_side_explicit.counter: (a) The self-heal is best-effort, not a guarantee. Two genuinely concurrent writers (analyst Mode 1 + analyst-baby, which CAN overlap — analyst-baby 04:20 vs analyst 04:00 are 20min apart and analyst runs are not instantaneous) racing in a gap window can each read next_id=627, both decide to allocate EXP-629, and both write EXP-629 with DIFFERENT bodies. The race window is small but the 21%-open staleness means there are ~44 windows/60d where it is open at all; the fix makes the window zero. (b) An EXP-629-with-two-bodies collision is UNRECOVERABLE without manual repair (unlike ISS, EXP carries a deliverable file + issue-proposals + tracker status — a silent double-allocation corrupts the integration chain). (c) PROP-089 set the discipline; extending it keeps id-allocation uniform across surfaces — per-surface ad-hoc defensive code is the 'I thought we fixed that' disaster shape the operator explicitly wants to avoid.
Q7_other_side_explicit.honest_recommendation: SHIP, but the operator should weigh (a) the rate is high (~5/week) which argues FOR the harden, against (b) the damage rate is zero-so-far which argues the self-heal is adequate. If the operator decides the noise cost of the strict gate exceeds the collision risk, the legitimate alternative is to DOWNGRADE the integrity next_id-inversion check to INFO and keep PROP-100's self-heal as the sole mechanism. This PROP makes the rate visible (Q3) precisely so the operator can make that call with eyes open. Tinker's lean: ship — the EXP collision is unrecoverable and the cost is one script + one lint + three hook lines.

Q8_phased_rollout.phase_0_shadow: Ship allocate-exp-ids.js + lint-exp-allocations.js in SHADOW. Writers call the script for allocation (real reserve-and-bump — this is safe and strictly better than improvising). The lint runs in REPORT-ONLY mode (logs would-have-aborted to monitor/integrity/exp-lint-shadow.jsonl, exit 0). EXIT criteria: >=5 runs of shadow data per writer (analyst, analyst-baby, decider) with zero divergent allocations vs the current ad-hoc path AND zero false-positive would-aborts on benign no_trace drift.
Q8_phased_rollout.phase_1_enforce: Enable the lint at push-time (exit 1 on violation) gated by presence of monitor/decisions/prop-106-enforce.flag — mirror the prop-009-enforce.flag convention. The hook reads the flag; absent = shadow, present = enforce.
Q8_phased_rollout.phase_2_retire: Remove the inline PROP-100 allocation blocks from the 4 prompt sites, leaving allocate-exp-ids.js as the sole entry point. The PROP-100 self-heal CLAMP stays (it now lives inside the script) — only the duplicated prose blocks are retired. Keep analyst-baby's defensive behavior as the Phase-0/Phase-1 safety net.

risks: Hook-on-three-agents: unlike PROP-089 (decider-only hook), this needs the lint chained into analyst + analyst-baby + decider pre-push hooks. More install surface. Mitigation: each agent's clone-setup section already installs hooks (PROP-081/083 pattern); add one chained invocation each.

Strict gate blocks summary-only commits when tracker is already stale from a prior bad write. This is intended (forces self-heal first) but could surprise a writer mid-run. Mitigation: C4 recovery procedure is a one-liner (re-run allocator to clamp), and shadow phase surfaces the frequency before enforce.

Script bypass remains possible for operator cowork sessions that hand-edit expansion-tracker.json — the lint only guards agent clones with the hook installed. Mitigation: CLAUDE.md note + integrity's daily next_id-inversion check stays as the final detector.

If the operator chooses the Q7 'downgrade integrity check instead' path, this PROP is shelved and PROP-100's self-heal remains sole mechanism — acceptable, the Q3 data supports an informed either-way call.
